title: YouTube Shorts Ads from Product Photos | AIVideosUGC
description: Make YouTube Shorts ads from a product photo or a product link. Pick an AI actor, a voice, and 6, 10, 15 or 30 seconds, then see the cost first.
h1: YouTube Shorts Ads from a Photo or a Link
lead: Open a YouTube Shorts ad on the product, not on a logo, so the first second earns the watch. Name the product after that move.
card: YouTube Shorts ads from a photo or a product link, in the tall shape Shorts uses.

faq.q: What should a YouTube Shorts ad feel like?
faq.a: A hand setting the product down and saying who it is for, with an [AI actor](/ai-video-generation/ai-actors) you can revoice. It is a tall Short.

faq.q: Can a Short earn more of the watch?
faq.a: A product opening is easier to stay with than a logo opening. If fewer people skip, you will see that in YouTube. We do not promise a longer watch.

faq.q: Is this a cheaper way to produce Shorts?
faq.a: Yes. You pay credits for each Short. A video is 24, 40, 60, or 120 credits for 6, 10, 15, or 30 seconds. Starter is $24.50 a month for 200 credits, Pro is $35 for 300, and Premium is $63 for 600.

faq.q: Will the person on camera look like a drawing?
faq.a: The mouth meets the words, and the eyes stay on the product. The voice can sit in an accent you pick. If YouTube asks you to say the person is AI, say it.

faq.q: Can I fix the words after I see the person?
faq.a: Yes. Rewrite the line after you see the avatar, then download.

faq.q: Will YouTube accept an AI Short as an ad?
faq.a: It can, if the product in the video is the product you ship and you say so when YouTube asks. We do not send the ad in. Read the disclosure rules on the day you publish.

faq.q: Does a Short start from a product link?
faq.a: Yes. The product page can start the YouTube Shorts ad. If you also need the wide player ad, render that shape on its own. Do not crop the Short and call it a player ad.
Use [social media ad sizes](/guides/ad-sizes-by-platform) before you download, and keep the product away from the buttons on the player.

benefits_h2: Why YouTube Shorts Ads Skip the Booking

benefits.d: You can run a hand on the product, a close-up, and a voice naming one fact, then spend the afternoon in the ad account instead of booking a studio.
When an angle goes quiet, you can make a new YouTube Shorts ad that starts with the product in use, without booking another shoot.
The next YouTube Shorts ad uses a photo that is already on the product page. You do not wait for a rented studio to open.

reasons.h2: What You Can Change on a YouTube Shorts Ad
reasons.lead: A second face on your YouTube Shorts ad does not require a second booking.

items.d: You can put a different face on the next YouTube Shorts ad, a navy hoodie after a grey tank, so the channel is not one face on repeat. You do not send a casting call.
Buyers can hear the line in a Texas accent, not a neutral read. That is the voice you pick for this account.
You keep the opening people stay with and retire the one they skip. The choice is yours after both have run.

reviews.h2: How shops use YouTube Shorts ads
reviews.lead: A few ways shops open a Short from one product.

items.d: A kitchen shop uses a pan photo for one cook motion, with the handle kept visible.

items.t: A color swipe, then the tube
items.d: A beauty shop uses a gloss photo for a swipe of color, with the tube still visible.
An electronics shop uses an earbud case photo and shows the open case in a hand.
A drink seller uses a can photo for a short pour, with the label facing the camera.
A home shop uses a lamp photo for a switch-on, so the shade shape is easy to see.
A fitness shop uses a mat photo for an unroll, so the length is easy to see.
An apparel shop uses a jacket photo for one zip, with the collar kept visible.
A pet shop uses a brush photo for a short grooming pass so the size is easy to see.
A jewelry shop uses a necklace photo for a clasp close-up, with the chain fully visible.
An outdoor shop uses a bottle photo for a sip, so the logo stays easy to read.
